questions.stem: In the deep cortical region of the lymph node labeled the paracortex in this diagram, which lymphocyte population predominates?

explanation.summary: The paracortex (deep cortex) is the T-cell zone of the lymph node, whereas the follicles of the outer cortex contain predominantly B cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The paracortex (deep cortex) is the T-cell zone of the lymph node, whereas the follicles of the outer cortex contain predominantly B cells.

questions.stem: This chest radiograph shows symmetric enlargement of both hilar regions (arrows) in a young adult. Which condition is the most likely underlying cause of this pattern?

explanation.summary: Bilateral, symmetric hilar lymphadenopathy in a young adult is the classic radiographic finding of the granulomatous disease sarcoidosis. Malignancies and infections more often cause asymmetric or unilateral adenopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bilateral, symmetric hilar lymphadenopathy in a young adult is the classic radiographic finding of the granulomatous disease sarcoidosis. Malignancies and infections more often cause asymmetric or unilateral adenopathy.
